newsitem.title: POLAND: ECHO, FRENCH, DUTCH FIRMS TO BUILD HOTELS.
newsitem.headline: ECHO, FRENCH, DUTCH FIRMS TO BUILD HOTELS.

text.p: The Polish developer Echo Investment SA has created a joint-stock company with French and Dutch hotel firms to build 100 budget-class hotels at the cost of some $350 million, Echo said in a statement on Monday.
The statement said Echo held 50 percent of the 12.5-million-zloty share capital in the new company called Hekon-Hotele Ekonomiczne SA.

The statement did not specify what stakes belonged to the French Societe de Promotion d'Hotellerie et de Restauration Economiques - Sphere International of Courcouronnes, a subsidiary of Accor Group, and the Dutch Copron BV of Rotterdam.
"The new company aims to build 100 budget hotels in Poland over the next five years. They would be managed by the French side," the statement said.
"The value of the investment is estimated by Echo at about $350 million," it said.
The French Accor Group runs over 2,000 budget hotels world wide under the names of Formule 1, Etap Hotel and Ibis Hotel.
Hekon-Hotele Ekonomiczne SA will be allowed to use the brand names Formule 1 for zero to one-star class hotels, Etap for one- to two-star hotels and Ibis for three-star hotels.

"Observing the rate of Poland's economic growth and the dramatic underdevelopment of the budget hotel base in Poland, Echo Investment has decided to direct its activity to create a network of budget hotels accessible to clients of different wealth," Echo said.
The Polish network of hotels will be incorporated into the world wide network of hotels offered to clients by Accor Group, the statement added.
